channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Aurora ADTP Blocks Ransomware with AI in Real Time
item.description: Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection (ADTP) employs AI‑powered intent detection to identify ransomware and advanced threats before they reach endpoints. The system analyzes traffic patterns and user behavior, flagging malicious payloads and command‑and‑control communications with high accuracy. Security teams should integrate ADTP into existing SIEM pipelines and enable real‑time alerting to maintain continuous protection.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Low‑Impact DHCP Security Update
item.description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 receives a DHCP security update addressing multiple bugs and enhancements. The advisory rates the update as Low impact, with CVSS scores linked to individual CVE references for detailed severity. Administrators should apply the latest dhcp package via yum or dnf to ensure patched configurations and mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: CVE-2026-124848: Kiro CLI Default Permissions Expose Sessions
item.description: CVE-2026-124848 reveals that Kiro CLI versions before 2.27.0 create session transcript files with world‑readable permissions on macOS and Linux. The flaw allows any local user to read credentials, source code, and other sensitive data stored in the prompt history, potentially enabling credential theft. Users should upgrade to Kiro CLI 2.27.0 or later, or manually change file permissions to restrict access.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for Enterprise Linux 9
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 9 addressing multiple security issues. Product Security rated the update as Important, and CVSS base scores are provided for each CVE linked in the references. Security teams should apply the patch promptly to mitigate the identified kernel vulnerabilities, maintain system integrity, and ensure compliance with security policies.

item.title: RHSA-2026:97539: Important: cockpit-machines security update
item.description: An update for cockpit-machines is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
item.description: A threat actor used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials for a Qubole big data platform's AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' AWS environments. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-126087.

item.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
item.description: A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index.

item.title: Microsoft Aware of Exploited Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194
item.description: Microsoft reports active exploitation of Outlook zero‑day CVE‑2026‑124194, found among 1,094 vulnerabilities patched in its November 2026 update. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution via malformed email attachments, scoring CVSS 10.0 and enabling arbitrary code on affected systems. Microsoft released a patch in the November 2026 Rollup; administrators should apply it immediately and monitor mail traffic for anomalous attachments.

item.title: SGLang RCE Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data
item.description: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, running arbitrary code on a NEAR AI inference server. The breach exposed data from 18 agents and about 100 users, including confidential requests processed in a trusted execution environment. NEAR AI applied a patch to SGLang and recommends updating to the latest version while monitoring logs for anomalous activity.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2027 , (Tue, Nov 10th)
item.description: Microsoft continues its AI-induced patch surge, addressing 1,260 different vulnerabilities this month. 167 of the vulnerabilities are Chromium issues affecting Microsoft Edge. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-113971.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Outlook Zero-Day
item.description: Microsoft released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday, addressing 1,235 vulnerabilities, including the actively exploited Outlook zero‑day CVE‑2026‑113971. The CVE permits unauthenticated remote code execution via malformed email attachments, scoring CVSS 10.0 and enabling arbitrary code execution. Administrators should apply the November 2026 Rollup immediately and verify that Outlook clients are updated to mitigate the vulnerability.

item.title: November 2026 Security Update Review
item.description: The November 2026 Security Update Review covers patch releases from Microsoft and Adobe, detailing record‑breaking vulnerability counts across products. Microsoft fixed 1,235 flaws, including an actively exploited Outlook zero‑day, while Adobe issued nine bulletins for 110 unique CVEs in its creative suite. Teams should apply the November 2026 Rollup, review Adobe bulletin IDs, and monitor for unpatched vulnerabilities.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,093 Vulnerabilities, Outlook Zero-Day
item.description: Microsoft released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates, fixing 1,093 vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, SQL Server, SharePoint, Exchange Server, Azure services, and developer tools. The update includes CVE-2026-113971, an actively exploited Outlook zero‑day that leaks users’ NTLMv2 authentication hashes to attackers. Security teams must apply the patch immediately to eliminate the credential theft vector and protect enterprise authentication infrastructure.

item.title: CVE-2026-126087 - Untrusted search path in OpenJD Sessions for Python and the AWS Deadline Cloud worker agent
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-177-AWS Publication Date: 11/10/2026 10:45 AM PST Description: Untrusted search path in the cross-user process launcher in Open Job Description (OpenJD) Sessions for Python before 0.11.0, as used in the AWS Deadline Cloud worker agent before 0.33.0, on Linux might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to submit jobs to a queue to execute arbitrary code as the worker agent OS user and obtain the AWS credentials held by the worker agent via a crafted job that modifies the PATH environment variable.

item.title: AI Coding Agents Leak Thousands of Secrets to GitHub
item.description: A command in Claude Code inadvertently saves files containing credentials and sensitive data to public Git repositories, creating security exposure for organizations. The leaked secrets include API keys, tokens, and authentication credentials that were committed to public repositories without authorization. Organizations must audit their AI coding agent configurations and implement pre-commit hooks to prevent credential leakage.

item.title: GStreamer Good Plugins Vulnerabilities Allow Remote Code Execution
item.description: Ubuntu 16.04, 18.04, and 20.04 are affected by GStreamer Good Plugins flaws (CVE-2026-3083, CVE-2026-3085, CVE-2026-39043) that mishandle network streams, Matroska, and WAV files. The vulnerabilities enable remote attackers to trigger crashes or potentially execute arbitrary code, posing a significant risk to affected systems. Apply Ubuntu security updates or upgrade GStreamer to a patched version to mitigate exploitation risk.

item.title: Microsoft Releases Windows 11 Cumulative Updates KB5132061, KB5131087
item.description: Microsoft released cumulative updates KB5132061 and KB5131087 for Windows 11 versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2. The updates address multiple security vulnerabilities and bugs, though specific CVE identifiers are not disclosed in the release notes. Users should install the patches via Windows Update or manually to maintain system security and feature parity.

item.title: Grafana Update Addresses Security Issues on RHEL9
item.description: Red Hat released a Grafana update for RHEL 9, addressing multiple security vulnerabilities. The advisory rates the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to CVE references, indicating medium‑to‑high severity flaws that could allow unauthorized data access. Administrators should apply the update promptly to mitigate potential exploitation and maintain system integrity.

item.title: edk2 Update for RHEL10 Addresses Low‑Severity Issues
item.description: Red Hat released an edk2 update for RHEL 10, targeting low‑severity security bugs that could affect firmware initialization. The advisory lists CVSS base scores linked to CVE references, indicating minimal exploitation risk. Users should apply the update to maintain firmware stability, though no immediate threat is reported, and monitor for any related advisories.

item.title: BYOD Ransomware Allegedly Claims Toyota Data Breach
item.description: The BYOD ransomware group claims it obtained personal information and kiosk device access from Toyota, though the claim remains unverified. No evidence confirms Toyota systems were breached or files were encrypted. Security teams should monitor threat actor claims and validate any reported data exposure through independent forensic analysis.

item.title: Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass Exploited for Admin Access
item.description: Hackers exploit a critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra to gain administrative privileges. The flaw, tracked as VSA-2026-062, parses authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into an empty object, enabling unauthorized access and is actively exploited, potentially compromising entire systems. Vates VMS urges immediate patch deployment and temporary disabling of unused REST endpoints to mitigate risk.

item.title: Adobe Fixes 110 Vulnerabilities in Nine Products
item.description: Adobe has patched 110 vulnerabilities across nine products, including AEM, Premiere, Photoshop, After Effects, Connect, Audition, Dimension, Content Credentials SDK, and Media Encoder. The flaws span configuration, input validation, and privilege escalation paths, but no active exploitation reports were disclosed. Adobe recommends applying the latest security updates immediately to mitigate potential risks.

item.title: Firefox Free VPN Drops 50GB Launch Cap Until January 31
item.description: Mozilla removed the data cap on the built-in Firefox free VPN, extending unlimited desktop and Android usage for users with a Mozilla account. The VPN protects traffic only inside Firefox and does not affect other applications on the device. Users benefit from unrestricted browsing without additional subscription costs beyond the existing Mozilla account requirement.

item.title: Git Addresses Six Security Vulnerabilities in Updates
item.description: Git released updates addressing six security vulnerabilities that affected recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports. The defects involve improper validation of repository metadata and could enable unauthorized code injection or data leakage. Users should install the latest Git version or apply the provided patches to secure their repositories.

item.title: China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked via Sparrow Malware
item.description: Three distinct threat clusters sharing infrastructure and malware code similarities have targeted telecommunications providers, government entities, military organizations, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe over the past year. Check Point Research tracks these clusters under names SilentDelivery and related designations.

item.title: Railway Exposes AI‑Driven API Key Theft and Charges
item.description: Railway disclosed that attackers leveraged AI agents, a build system flaw, and cloud misconfigurations to exfiltrate customer API keys. The compromised secrets enabled the adversary to generate approximately $740,000 in unauthorized cloud charges across multiple internal systems. Railway is tightening build pipelines, enforcing stricter access controls, and monitoring for anomalous API usage to prevent future incidents.

item.title: Notion Confirms AI Chat Transcripts Exposed in Fireworks AI Breach, Affecting Customer Workspaces
item.description: Notion has confirmed that a security incident at Fireworks AI exposed Notion AI chat transcripts linked to fewer than 1% of its customer workspaces. Insights, a feature that helps teams understand their AI usage, used the affected conversations.

item.title: SBOM, AI BOMs Drive New Software Transparency
item.description: Allan Friedman discussed how SBOMs and emerging AI BOMs are reshaping software supply‑chain visibility. He emphasized that knowing component contents is only the first step, and organizations must analyze SBOM data to detect risks. The podcast recommends adopting automated SBOM ingestion tools and integrating AI analysis to prioritize remediation efforts.

item.title: Ivanti Issues Patches for Endpoint Manager, CSA Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ivanti released patches for Endpoint Manager, Endpoint Manager Mobile, Sentry, and Cloud Services Application after discovering flaws enabling remote code execution, certificate tampering, data exposure, and service disruption. Two critical vulnerabilities in Endpoint Manager and Cloud Services Application pose the highest risk, requiring code execution privileges. Administrators should apply the updates immediately and verify certificate trust chains to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: CVE‑2026‑125271: AWS API MCP Policy Bypass
item.description: CVE‑2026‑125271 exposes a policy bypass in AWS API MCP Server caused by incorrect operation name normalization. The flaw allows actors to execute operations that the operator's security policy denies or requires elicitation for, potentially granting unauthorized API access. AWS has released a patch for affected versions (>=0.2.13); administrators should update immediately and review policy configurations.

item.title: Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass Enables VM Server Hijack
item.description: A critical authentication bypass flaw in Xen Orchestra is actively exploited to grant admin privileges and seize XCP‑ng virtualization hosts. The flaw bypasses login checks, giving attackers full control over host management interfaces, and is used in multiple attacks. Xen Orchestra issued an urgent patch; administrators should apply it immediately and audit host authentication logs for anomalies.

item.title: Fireworks Reports Data Theft During October Breaches
item.description: AI company Fireworks disclosed that hackers stole data and billing information during October incidents affecting a limited number of customer accounts. All affected customers were notified of the attack. The company should conduct forensic investigation to determine scope and implement enhanced access monitoring for sensitive billing records.

item.title: Benchmarking Offensive AI Agent Capabilities
item.description: The article presents a framework for assessing AI agents' cybersecurity capabilities, focusing on offensive testing. It outlines the construction of the Wiz Cyber Model Arena, detailing scenario design, adversarial objectives, and performance metrics. The authors recommend iterative validation, data collection, and continuous improvement to ensure robust evaluation for security teams.

item.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy Sandbox-Evading Python Backdoor
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an attack that exploited two now-patched vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS to deliver a Python-based implant. The activity, observed by Huntress in October 2026, involves the exploitation of a chain comprising CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on affected systems.

item.title: Microsoft Acknowledges Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation
item.description: Microsoft acknowledges CVE-2026-69898, a critical Windows kernel privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow local users to gain elevated privileges. The update is purely informational, with no evidence of active exploitation, public proof‑of‑concept, or a released patch. No remediation guidance is provided, and security teams should monitor Microsoft advisories for future updates.

item.title: Azure DevOps Server RCE Exploited via Improper Auth
item.description: CVE-2026-109467 is a remote code execution flaw in Azure DevOps Server that lets authenticated attackers run arbitrary code over the network. The issue arises from improper authentication handling in the REST API, allowing credential bypass and code execution with elevated privileges. Microsoft released a patch; administrators should apply it immediately and audit access controls to mitigate risk.

item.title: HEIF Image Extensions Vulnerability Enables Local RCE
item.description: A use‑after‑free flaw in Microsoft HEIF Image Extensions lets an unauthorized attacker execute code locally on Windows. CVE‑2026‑100204 exploits heap corruption triggered by a crafted HEIF file, enabling local code execution without authentication. Microsoft released a patch in the latest cumulative update; apply it immediately or disable HEIF processing as a temporary fix.

item.title: Windows Kernel Use-After-Free Allows Local Privilege Escalation
item.description: A use‑after‑free bug in the Windows Kernel allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally on affected systems. The flaw, identified as CVE‑2026‑108403, arises from improper memory handling during kernel operations, enabling local privilege escalation without authentication. Microsoft has issued a patch in the latest cumulative update; administrators should apply it promptly to prevent privilege escalation.

item.title: ODBC Driver Heap Overflow Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: A heap‑based buffer overflow in the Microsoft ODBC Driver permits an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network. CVE‑2026‑108411 exploits memory corruption triggered by malformed ODBC requests, enabling remote code execution without authentication. Microsoft released a patch in the latest cumulative update; apply it immediately or restrict ODBC traffic as a temporary workaround.

item.title: Windows DNS RCE via Deserialization Vulnerability
item.description: Microsoft disclosed CVE-2026-109463, a deserialization flaw in Windows DNS enabling unauthenticated remote code execution over the network. Attackers can craft malicious DNS responses to trigger arbitrary code execution on affected systems. Microsoft released an emergency patch addressing this critical vulnerability, and administrators should deploy it promptly to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets
item.description: Binance is warning about a vulnerability in Apple's iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 that could allow third-party apps to read private files stored by other apps, including cryptocurrency seed phrases, secret keys, and login credentials.
